description: "What's the ticker for..." / "find the CIK for..." / "what's the LEI for..." / "what's the RxCUI for..." / "look up the ID for..." / "what is X's official identifier" / "who owns X" / "is X a subsidiary of Y", resolve a user-spoken NAME to the canonical/official identifiers other tools require as input. Use FIRST whenever you have a name but need an ID. SUPPORTED TYPES: "company" (cross-source identity spine: 10-digit CIK + ticker + company_name from SEC EDGAR, legal-entity LEI from GLEIF with p

country.description: OPTIONAL ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the country whose business register you mean ("NO", "FI", "JP", "GB", "FR", "EE", "BR"). Narrows the national-register fan-out and is often the difference between the right company and a US namesake, "Apple" with country "NO" is a Norwegian company, not Apple Inc. Omitting it searches every register we can name, which is the right default when you do not know. A bare number with a non-US country is that country's register number, never read as an SEC CIK (a 10-digit number still is). company only; ignored for drug.

type.description: Entity type: "company", "drug" or "lei" (a 20-character LEI; "company" also recognises an LEI by its check digits).

value.description: For company: ticker (AAPL), CIK (0000320193 or 320193), LEI (HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394), or name. A bare number is read as an SEC CIK only as 320193 or 0000320193; with a non-US `country`, or with 8-9 digits starting with 0 (a Companies House number), it is not a CIK and is not asserted as one. A bare number of 7 digits or fewer sent without `country` is always read as an SEC CIK, so a short register number (for example an Irish CRO or a US state filing number) that equals a real CIK will resolve to that SEC filer; send a non-US `country` with a foreign register number. A US state filing number cannot be resolved by number; search by company name instead. For drug: brand or generic name (e.g., "ozempic", "metformin"). Pass the ENTITY NAME ONLY, for a bond that is the ISSUER exactly as printed ("NEW YORK ST DORM AUTH"), never the question's full noun phrase ("NEW YORK ST DORM AUTH revenue bonds"): the FIGI lookup matches instrument names, so trailing security-class words match nothing.
